I am an old woman, almost seventy years, and this small piece of land behind my house is where I plant my yam and cassava like my mother taught me. I have no money for the fertilizer from the shop, and my plot is too small for one bag anyway — I just throw the goat droppings and kitchen ash on the mounds like I always do. I keep my own yam seed from last harvest and cassava cuttings from my sister's farm, that is what we use here. My back is not strong like before, so my daughter comes to help me weed, and if the work is too much I will beg my grandson to cut the bush for small money.
